written.myAnswer: Most metals have strong metallic bonds, giving them high melting points, so they are solids at room temperature. Non-metals generally have weaker bonding and a wider range of melting points, so they may be gases or solids at room temperature.

Metal atoms are held together by strong metallic bonds, making metals generally tough and strong. Non-metals generally have weaker bonding and are brittle, so they break rather than deform when force is applied.

Metals are generally lustrous, malleable, ductile, tough and strong, and conduct heat and electricity well. Non-metals are generally dull, brittle, neither tough nor strong, and poor conductors; they may be solids, liquids or gases at room temperature. There are exceptions, such as conducting graphite, lustrous iodine and liquid mercury.
